answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to post a refundable stake that rises along a spiral of reputation: new identities start below a low trust ridge they must climb through verified useful work before handling valuable transactions. Colluding identities that attest each other are detected because their interaction graph looks like karst, full of hollow disconnected cavities with no shared history, and their stakes are slashed, so creating many fake agents costs more than the fraud can earn.
